summary: Import-time binary dropper fetches and executes attacker-controlled payload from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: On require() of accounts-final-form, index.js loads setup.js which schedules a bootstrap via process.nextTick. lib/telemetry.js downloads a platform-specific native binary (linux_x64 /pkg/package, darwin /pkg/loader_mac, win32 /pkg/package.exe) from a hardcoded pool of Cloudflare Workers subdomains (package-proxy.cf5oob.worker.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf8oob.worker.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf12oob.worker.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf17-ddb.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf25-6eb.workers.dev) with DNS fallbacks under well1.site (tin/tina/ldr/win.dl.well1.site), writes the binary to /var/tmp (or %TEMP% on Windows), chmods it 755, and executes it. Destination hostnames and sensitive API identifiers are assembled from split string fragments at runtime (e.g. hostnames joined from arrays, os["plat"+"form"], fs["chmod"+"Sync"], require("child_"+"process")) to defeat literal-string scanning. setup.js also computes an install fingerprint from os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), process.version, and process.pid and sends it as installId alongside the payload fetch, enabling per-host tracking. The package is framed as an analytics SDK; the fetched binaries are opaque and unrelated to any declared publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
